editorial:
Based on a true story, this Korean drama follows a new teacher who arrives at a school for deaf children and slowly discovers that the students are being abused by the very people meant to protect them. You watch him team up with a human rights activist to fight for justice, but the system keeps pushing back. The tone is heavy and emotional, and the film does not look away from the pain these kids go through. You feel their silence and their fear in every scene.

The acting is strong across the board, especially from the young cast, and the pacing keeps you locked in even when the story gets hard to watch. On the downside, some scenes are very tough to sit through, and the ending may leave you frustrated with the justice system. This is best for viewers who want a powerful, eye-opening drama and can handle dark themes.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the teacher and activist take the case to court, hoping the abusers will be punished. Instead, the court gives them light sentences, and the school stays open. The teacher feels defeated but keeps fighting for the kids. The twist is that real life was even worse than the movie, and the film ends with a note about how the actual case led to new laws in Korea. You are left angry but hopeful that speaking up can still make a difference.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves powerful true-story dramas and can handle dark themes.
